cover.headline: A great franchise priced for a re-rating that its own history does not support: SELL
cover.lead: M&M is India's No.1 SUV maker by revenue (25% share), its largest tractor maker (44%) and the leader in small pickups (52%); it also owns 25% of Tech Mahindra, 52% of M&M Finance and 92% of its electric-SUV company, MEAL. The business has never been better run: standalone revenue tripled in five years and ROE is above 20%. But growth is slowing (we forecast EPS +{{F.epsGrowth.0|n1}}% in FY27 after +32% in FY26), a weak monsoon (87% of normal) threatens the tractor cycle, and EVs made for MEAL dilute margins. The street values M&M on a **sum of the parts**, and so do we: the auto and farm business at 12.5x Sep-28E core EPS (M&M's own median since 2021, 13.2x, cut 6.9% for the sector's de-rating) plus the stakes (listed at the 30-Sep price, unlisted at cost) less a 20% holding discount. **That gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Every broker we found rates it Buy or Hold (₹3,675-4,875). Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The franchise is excellent, and capacity will double
arguments.p: SUV revenue share 25%, e-SUV revenue share 44%, LCV <3.5T share 52%, tractor share 44.9% in Q1FY27. SUV capacity goes from 64.5k units a month at FY26 exit to 92k by FY28 and ~130k by FY31 (Nagpur). Management says demand, not supply, is the constraint today. We model domestic UVs +16% in FY27 and tractors +4%.

arguments.h: But profit growth is slowing to ~13% a year
arguments.p: Q1FY27 core EBITDA margin fell to 12.2% (14.3% a year earlier) on 400-500bp of commodity inflation. Price increases (1.5% + 2.7%) help, but e-SUVs built for MEAL at a ~0.4% margin rise from 11% to ~20% of auto revenue, tractors face a weak-monsoon year, and capex doubles. We forecast EBITDA margins of {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}} and EPS of {{F.eps.0|n1}} / {{F.eps.1|n1}} / {{F.eps.2|n1}} for FY27-29E.

arguments.h: The stock still prices the 2024-25 re-rating
arguments.p: Strip out the stakes and M&M's core business traded at 8-12x forward earnings in 2021-23 and 18-21x in 2024-25. Today it is 15.9x FY28E, above the 13.2x median since 2021, while auto-OEM peers trade 6.9% below their own five-year medians. The street's 22-26x multiples assume the re-rating is permanent; our rule does not.

arguments.h: The stakes are a cushion, not hidden upside
arguments.p: Listed stakes are worth ₹638 a share at the 30-Sep prices (Tech Mahindra ₹304, M&M Finance ₹191); with MEAL and other unlisted companies at cost the stakes add ₹816 gross, ₹653 after a 20% discount. MEAL's investors converted at ~₹40,400 cr in May-2026, half the ₹80,580 cr headline of 2023; valuing MEAL there adds only ~₹196 a share.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether auto margins recover from 12.2% as guided; tractor margins under steel and rubber inflation.
Festive season (Navratri from 11-October 2026) and rabi sowing after a monsoon at 87% of normal: the first read on tractor demand for H2FY27 and FY28.
Commodities and West Asia: every 100bp of standalone EBITDA margin is ~₹1,970 cr of FY28E EBITDA, ~7% of EPS.
Capacity: 68k SUVs a month from September 2026, 82k by March 2027; first NU_IQ and new INGLO models in FY28.
Group: truck and bus sale to SML (₹525 cr, FY27), Last Mile Mobility listing targeted for calendar 2027, MEAL investors' exit window from November 2027.

sections.title: Two businesses inside the listed company, a dozen more around it

blocks.p: Mahindra & Mahindra (the listed company, "standalone") makes SUVs, pickups and small trucks (automotive: 75% of FY26 revenue) and tractors, farm machinery and engines (farm: 25%). It sells e-SUVs too, but those are built in M&M's Chakan plant for MEAL, a 92.45% subsidiary that sells them under the XEV and BE names; M&M books the vehicle at full price and earns a thin manufacturing margin. Around the listed company sits the wider group: Tech Mahindra (IT services, 25.3% held, an associate), M&M Finance (vehicle and rural loans, 52.5%), Mahindra Lifespaces, Logistics, Holidays, SML (trucks and buses), Swaraj Engines, and unlisted companies such as Last Mile Mobility (3-wheelers), Aerostructures, Accelo (steel processing) and Susten (renewables).

sections.title: Three markets, three cycles: SUVs booming, tractors peaking, pickups steady

blocks.p: **SUVs.** India sold 46,43,439 passenger vehicles in FY26 (+7.9%), of which 31,05,025 were utility vehicles (+11%): two out of three. M&M's share of UVs rose from 17.2% (FY24) to 19.7% (FY25) and 21.3% (FY26). The GST reset of 22-Sep-2025 cut the tax on large SUVs from 28% plus 22% cess to a flat 40% and M&M cut prices by ₹81,000-1.56 lakh. April-August 2026 UV sales rose 30.7% to 13,62,527, but against a weak base: buyers held back in August-September 2025 waiting for the tax cut. M&M's UVs rose 22% in the same months (~21.6% of industry UVs), capped by capacity. Forecasters (CRISIL in May-2026: +5-7% for FY27) expect much slower growth once the base normalises.

**Tractors.** The industry sold 11,60,231 tractors in FY26 (+23.5%): +11.6% in April-August, then +31.2% after the GST cut in September 2025. Volumes have grown 8.2% a year since FY09, but in cycles: a weak monsoon usually brings a down year. The 2026 monsoon was 87% of the long-period average, the 4th weakest since 2001, with June at 65% and 17 of 36 sub-divisions deficient; central and north-west India (the big tractor markets) were close to normal (97% and 94.1%), the south (76%) and north-east (74%) were not. M&M sold 2,12,664 tractors in India in April-August 2026 (+17%) but only +5% in August, and retail sales were flat in August. Management guided mid-single-digit industry growth for FY27 in May.

**Pickups and small trucks.** LCVs under 3.5 tonnes: 5,11,401 units in FY26 (+9.4%), M&M 48.3% on SIAM's basis (52% on the company's). A steady, rural-linked market, helped by the GST cut on goods vehicles; management guides high-single-digit growth.

blocks.h: Five other forces that matter for M&M

bullets: **Commodities and West Asia:** crude touched ~$100 in March 2026; steel rose 24% and rubber 30% in calendar 2026 to July. M&M lost 400-500bp of auto margin and 300bp+ of farm margin in Q1FY27 before price increases.

**EVs:** industry e-SUV penetration reached ~9% in Q1FY27 (2-2.5% a few quarters earlier); M&M is at 12% and No.1 by e-SUV revenue (44%). The PLI subsidy supports margins and is expected to taper as scale builds. CAFE-III fuel-efficiency norms start in April 2027.

**Rare-earth magnets:** China's export curbs from April 2025 threatened EV motors; M&M said it was covered through March 2026 with stocked sub-assemblies and alternative sources, China eased curbs for India in August 2025, and India launched a ₹7,280 cr magnet scheme. No production loss was disclosed.

**Competition:** six credible SUV makers (Maruti, Tata, Hyundai, Kia, Toyota, M&M) plus new entrants (VinFast, BYD) and, after the India-EU trade deal of January 2026, cheaper European imports over time.

**Interest rates and rural credit:** most tractors and pickups are bought on loans (M&M Finance is a large lender to M&M customers); a weak monsoon raises credit costs and tightens lending in the following year.

sections.title: Tailwind test: M&M captures the SUV and EV shift; tractors are a cycle, not a trend

blocks.p: A sector tailwind helps shareholders only if the company captures it. We score each driver.

verdicts: UVs are two-thirds of PVs; M&M is No.1 by SUV revenue share (25%) and gained 4 points of UV volume share in two years.
The core of the investment case; capacity (not demand) limits volumes to FY28.
Large SUVs moved to 40% from ~50%; small cars to 18%. M&M passed on ₹81,000-1.56 lakh; tractors and pickups also got lower GST.
A one-time step-up in demand; FY27-28 compare against a high base.
M&M e-SUV penetration 12% vs industry 9%; No.1 by e-SUV revenue. But the profit sits in MEAL (92.45%), not in standalone M&M.
Positive for the group; neutral to slightly negative for standalone margins.
Labour shortages push farmers to tractors and implements; 69-70% of M&M's Q1FY27 mix is 40-50HP; farm machinery +17%.
A real long-term trend (8.2% CAGR since FY09) but around a volatile cycle.
FY26 and H1FY27 were strong; the 2026 monsoon was 87% of normal (El Nino).
The next 12-18 months are more likely a headwind than a tailwind.
Vehicle exports +63% in Apr-Aug 2026, but only ~5% of volume; tractor exports 4% of volume, with weak international subsidiaries (Turkey, Brazil, US).
400-500bp margin hit in Q1FY27; 4.2% of price increases since.
Pricing power exists, but with a lag of 1-2 quarters.

blocks.title: Tailwind scorecard: M&M captures 3 of 7 fully, 2 partly, and faces 2 headwinds

blocks.callout: **Our view:** M&M is the clearest beneficiary of India's SUV boom and is well placed for EVs. The tractor business is a high-quality franchise in a cyclical market, and FY26 was close to a peak. Our forecasts give the SUV tailwind full credit (domestic UVs +16% in FY27, +12% in FY28) and assume tractors flatten (+4% in FY27, −2% in FY28).

sections.title: Automotive: No.1 by SUV revenue, capacity-bound until FY28

blocks.p: M&M's automotive revenue rose from ₹25,014 cr in FY21 to ₹1,09,355 cr in FY26. Three things did it: a run of hit SUVs (XUV700 in 2021, Scorpio-N in 2022, Thar Roxx in 2024, the XUV 7XO refresh in 2026), price and mix (revenue per vehicle up from ~₹7 lakh to ~₹11 lakh including e-SUVs built for MEAL), and the GST cut. Segment PBIT margin rose from 4.8% in FY23 (AR FY24 comparatives) to 8.4% in FY24 and 9.3% in FY26. Q1FY27 was the first setback: margin 7.1% (8.9% for SUVs and pickups without e-SUVs) after 400-500bp of commodity inflation and an ~85bp hedging loss. Management took 1.5% and then a 2.7% average price increase (mid-July) and calls Q1 the low point.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** demand is not the problem: capacity is. We model domestic UVs +16% in FY27 (inside the 68-70k a month M&M can build) and +12% in FY28 as NU_IQ adds a new segment. The risk is margin: e-SUVs, which M&M builds for MEAL at ~0.4% PBIT, rise from 11% to ~21% of automotive revenue by FY29E, which mechanically pulls down the standalone margin even if each business does well.

sections.title: Farm: the best business in the group, at the top of its cycle

blocks.p: M&M has held 40-45% of India's tractor market for decades through two brands (Mahindra and Swaraj), with core tractor PBIT margins in a 17-21% band through up- and down-cycles. FY26 was a record: 5.26 lakh tractors (+24%), farm PBIT margin 19.8%. Q1FY27 volumes rose 18% (share 44.9%, down from a record 45.2% a year earlier); core tractor margin held at 19.2% despite steel (+24%) and rubber (+30%) inflation; farm PBIT including the loss-making international businesses was 18.5% standalone and 14.2% consolidated. The weak spots are abroad: Turkey (Erkunt Foundry exited with an impairment), Brazil and the US are in industry downturns, and Sampo (Finland) was sold in 2025.

pair.title: Farm PBIT margin near 20%: hard to beat

blocks.p: **Our forecast:** tractor volumes +4% in FY27 (April-August was +16%, so September-March is ~−2% against a base that grew 31% after the GST cut) and −2% in FY28, the year an El Nino monsoon usually hits rabi incomes, then +5% in FY29. Realisation +3% a year (a ₹15,000 price increase in August, more 40-50HP tractors, farm machinery). Farm revenue: ₹39,007 / 39,370 / 42,576 cr. Management guided mid-single-digit industry growth for FY27; a repeat of FY26 is not in our numbers.

blocks.callout: **Why it matters:** farm is ~25% of standalone revenue but ~40% of segment profit (FY26 PBIT ₹7,206 cr vs ₹10,141 cr in auto). A 10% fall in tractor volumes with 2 points lower margin would cut FY28E standalone EPS by ~6%: our bear case takes revenue growth 4 points lower and margins 1.5 points lower across the company.

sections.title: EVs: a profitable leader, owned through a subsidiary investors valued at half the headline

blocks.p: M&M's electric SUVs (BE 6, XEV 9e and, since late 2025, the XEV 9S) are sold by Mahindra Electric Automobile Ltd (MEAL), on M&M's INGLO platform, and built under contract in M&M's Chakan plant. MEAL sold 51,820 e-SUVs in FY26 and 19,540 in Q1FY27 (+77%): 12% of M&M's SUVs, against 9% for the industry, and No.1 by e-SUV revenue (44%). In Q1FY27 MEAL earned ₹5,430 cr of revenue at a 10.6% EBITDA margin (₹271 cr PBIT); M&M's contract manufacturing earned only ~0.4%. Management says MEAL is EBITDA positive even without the PLI subsidy; FY26 PAT was ₹387 cr.

blocks.p: **How we value it.** BII and Temasek invested ₹3,050 cr through convertible shares at headline valuations of ₹70,070 cr and ₹80,580 cr. On 1-May-2026 they converted into 4.58% and 2.97% of MEAL, the top of their ranges, which implies a post-money value of only ~₹40,400 cr: the performance-linked formula did not deliver the headline. M&M has invested ₹6,950 cr and has approved ₹15,925 cr in total. Investors may seek an exit from November 2027 (a listing or a sale). In our base case MEAL is at M&M's cost (₹6,950 cr), the same basis as our multiple history; at the conversion value it would add ~₹196 a share (our bull case).

blocks.callout: **Brutal honesty:** EVs are M&M's best strategic asset but not yet a big profit pool. MEAL's ₹387 cr FY26 profit is ~2% of group profit, it relies on PLI support that management expects to taper, and its outside investors converted at half the headline value. The bull case on M&M is not about MEAL alone.

sections.title: The stakes: ₹816 a share gross, mostly Tech Mahindra and M&M Finance

blocks.p: M&M's listed stakes were worth ₹79,392 cr at the 30-Sep-2026 closes, ₹638 a share: Tech Mahindra (24.8 cr shares at ₹1,524) and M&M Finance (73.0 cr shares at ₹324.85) are 78% of it. Group companies paid M&M ₹1,769 cr of dividends in FY26, most of it from these two. GAM rates Tech Mahindra SELL (target ₹1,430) and M&M Finance HOLD (₹330); at those targets the stakes would be worth ~₹16 a share less. Unlisted companies are carried at cost (₹17,625 cr after ₹7,101 cr of write-downs), and we add ₹4,500 cr for new investment by Sep-27E.

blocks.h: The holding discount: history cannot pin it down, and it barely matters

blocks.p: The market price is one number; it cannot tell us both what investors pay for the core business and what discount they apply to the stakes. So we take the street's 20% (ICICI Direct uses 20-25%) and derive the core multiple from M&M's own history on the same 20%. Because both are on one basis, the target hardly moves with the discount: a bigger discount lowers the stakes but raises the core multiple history implies.

blocks.callout: **Capital allocation:** since 2021 management has exited loss-makers (SsangYong, Sampo, Erkunt), set an 18% ROE hurdle and paid out ~26% of profit. But the parent keeps funding group companies (₹6,398 cr in FY26; ₹8,975 cr still committed to MEAL) and wrote down ₹1,778 cr of them in FY24-26. We treat that money as worth its cost, no more.

blocks.p: **Verdict: a wide moat in tractors and small pickups, a narrow one in SUVs.** Tractors and pickups are rural, finance-dependent, service-heavy businesses where M&M's dealer reach, resale values and M&M Finance give it a durable lead: share has stayed in the 40s for decades. In SUVs the lead is product-led: it was won with the XUV700/Scorpio-N/Thar cycle and must be re-won with every model; Maruti (No.1 by volume), Tata and Hyundai-Kia are all investing. In EVs M&M is ahead today, but a platform lead in a market at 9% penetration with falling battery costs is not yet a moat.

blocks.callout: **So what:** the moat justifies a premium to mass-market carmakers, which is why we value the core on M&M's own history rather than on a peer average. It does not justify assuming that the 2024-25 multiple is the new normal.

sections.title: Five years of 25% compounding, now slowing to ~13%

blocks.p: Standalone M&M (the auto and farm businesses, without the group companies) earned ₹{{fin.pat.5|num}} cr in FY20 and ₹{{fin.pat.11|num}} cr in FY26. The early years are distorted by write-downs of group companies (SsangYong in FY20-21, trucks in FY23), so the cleaner comparison is revenue and operating profit. Revenue went from ₹{{fin.sales.6|num}} cr in FY21 to ₹{{fin.sales.11|num}} cr in FY26 (27% a year), as SUVs (XUV700, Scorpio-N, Thar Roxx, XUV 3XO) and a GST-cut tractor boom arrived on top of each other. EBITDA (operating profit) margin, measured without dividends from group companies, rose from 12.2% in FY22 to {{fin.ebitdaMargin.10|pct}} in FY25 and {{fin.ebitdaMargin.11|pct}} in FY26, then fell to 12.2% in Q1FY27 when commodities jumped.

bullets: **Margins:** Auto absorbed 400-500bp of commodity inflation in Q1 (escalated after Feb-2026 with the West Asia conflict) and an ~85bp hedging loss in the last 10 days of June when commodities fell on news the war was stopping; farm 300-400bp (steel +24%, rubber +30% YTD, unhedgeable). Price increases: auto ~1.5% (spring) + 2.7% average (mid-Jul-2026); tractors ~Rs15,000 per unit (Aug).

**Guidance:** Auto: Q1 is the low point; Q2 operating margin maintained or slightly better if commodities hold. Farm: temporary pressure in Q2 (commodities, festival shift to 11-Oct). FY27 (Q4FY26 call, May-2026): M&M UV growth mid-to-high teens, tractor industry mid-single digits, LCV industry high single digits. Capacity, not demand, is the constraint in SUVs.

**Capacity:** Operational SUV capacity 64.5k/month at FY26 exit (56.5k ICE + 8k BEV), 68k by Sep-2026, 82k by Mar-2027 (14k of it for FY28 launches), 92k by FY28 exit (NU_IQ phase 2 at Chakan), Nagpur greenfield 20k/month by H1CY29 and another 20k ~12 months later: 2x in five years (FY26-FY31 exit).
**Group:** M&M Finance PAT +78% (GS3 3.45%), Tech Mahindra PAT +28% (EBIT margin 14.4%), "growth gems" PAT 3x; consolidated ROE 23%.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** the quarter showed strong demand and good cost control, but also how exposed margins are to commodities; management's "Q1 is the low point" depends on commodities not rising again. Since the call, M&M's domestic UVs grew 50% in August (on a weak pre-GST-cut base) and tractors only 5%.

sections.title: Earnings quality: good cash conversion, but read the reported revenue with care

bullets: From FY23 'income from investments related to subsidiaries, associates and JVs' (dividends, interest on loans to group companies, stake-sale gains: Rs2,190 cr in FY26) is shown inside total income from operations, and 'loss from investments' (write-downs: Rs677 cr in FY26) inside expenses. We move both out (M&M.patch.js) so revenue and EBITDA are the operating business only.
e-SUVs are built by M&M and sold to MEAL at full vehicle value (Rs12,413 cr in FY26) at a ~0.4% PBIT margin: this inflates standalone revenue growth and dilutes the standalone margin as EVs grow.
Impairments of group investments recur: Rs3,087 cr (FY21), Rs1,430 cr (FY23), Rs253/848/677 cr (FY24-26); cumulative impairment Rs7,101 cr at Mar-26.
PLI incentives for EVs (Rs1,371 cr of 'government grants and incentives' in FY26 revenue, all schemes) support EV profitability; management says MEAL is EBITDA positive without PLI.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing we found is aggressive, and cash conversion is strong (negative working capital). But three things make the reported numbers look better than the operating business: dividends from group companies shown inside revenue (₹2,190 cr in FY26), e-SUVs booked at full value for a ~0.4% margin, and a steady stream of write-downs of group companies that the company treats as exceptional. Our core EPS strips all three.

sections.title: Net cash of ~₹31,000 cr, plus ₹27,500 cr of group companies at cost

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 standalone M&M had ₹32,965 cr of liquid funds (bank deposits ₹17,719 cr, cash ₹761 cr, mutual funds and bonds ₹14,485 cr) against ₹1,653 cr of debt (incl. ₹597 cr of leases): net cash ~₹31,300 cr, ~₹252 a share. It also carried ₹27,547 cr of investments in group companies at cost after ₹7,101 cr of cumulative write-downs; their market value is far higher (the listed ones alone were worth ₹70,476 cr at Mar-2026). Working capital is negative: suppliers fund M&M (payables ₹29,500 cr vs inventory ₹10,306 cr and receivables ₹6,486 cr). Our view

blocks.p: Brokers that disclose a method use a sum of the parts: the standalone business on P/E (Motilal Oswal 24x autos / 26x tractors on Mar-28E; Anand Rathi 22x Mar-28E EPS incl. MEAL; Choice 25x FY28E EPS) or EV/EBITDA (ICICI Direct 15x FY28E), plus listed subsidiaries at market or house targets and others at investment value, less a 20-25% holding discount. We use the same structure: (1) the standalone auto and farm business, including its own cash, on P/E on Sep-28E core EPS (₹155.9: standalone EPS excluding one-offs and the dividends and other income from group companies); (2) listed stakes at the 30-Sep-2026 close; (3) unlisted group companies at M&M's investment (cost net of write-downs), plus new investment to Sep-27E; (4) a 20% holding discount on (2) and (3). blocks.p: Tata Motors demerged on 1-Oct-2025: TMPV (the old listing, now passenger vehicles + JLR) carries a P/E history that includes the CV business and a demerger gain, and TMCV listed only on 12-Nov-2025, so neither has a usable five-year median; both are left out of the de-rating and shown for reference only. Escorts Kubota's trailing EPS at 30-Sep no longer includes the June-2025 gain on selling its railway business, so we keep it (its de-rating, −39%, is the market's view of the tractor cycle). M&M's own headline P/E (price ÷ trailing standalone EPS) is 15% below its five-year median, but that comparison flatters it: trailing EPS includes ~₹2,000 cr a year of dividends from group companies and the stakes themselves are worth ~₹653 a share.

blocks.callout: **So what:** the sector is ~7% cheaper than usual, Maruti (−17%) and Escorts (−39%) most. That is the de-rating we apply. M&M's core is not cheap on its own history (15.9x vs 13.2x); it only looks cheap against peers' absolute multiples, which is why the street's 22-26x targets come from comparisons with Maruti and Eicher rather than with M&M's past.

sections.title: Our honest summary: own the business, not at this price

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's best-placed SUV and tractor maker, with net cash of ~₹31,000 cr, capacity doubling by FY31 and the e-SUV lead; plus ₹816 a share of group companies (Tech Mahindra and M&M Finance are 61% of it). Management has a credible record since 2021: exits from loss-makers, ROE above 20%.

**What you are paying:** ₹2,950 is 15.9x FY28E core earnings after deducting the stakes, against 13.2x over five years; the whole company is {{V.pe.current|x}} trailing standalone earnings. EPS growth of ~13% a year from here does not need a 22-26x multiple. Our sum of the parts gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).

statementNotes.materialPct@FY22: Material cost ratio up 6 points: steel and precious-metal inflation and the auto recovery (farm back to 36% of revenue).
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY22: Margin 12.2% (−340bp): commodity inflation ahead of price increases.
statementNotes.otherIncome@FY22: Back to normal: no large write-downs; dividends from group companies.
statementNotes.pat@FY22: Profit +395% on a FY21 base depressed by the SsangYong write-off.
statementNotes.sales@FY23: Revenue +47%: Scorpio-N, XUV700 at scale, vehicles sold +50%, tractors +15%.
statementNotes.materialPct@FY23: Auto rose to 70% of segment revenue (64% in FY22); commodities stayed high.
statementNotes.dep@FY23: D&A +26%: new SUV platforms (XUV700, Scorpio-N) amortised as they launched.
statementNotes.otherIncome@FY23: Exceptional loss ₹1,430 cr (trucks impairment net of Susten/SEL gains) and ₹63 cr loss from investments; ₹1,684 cr of group income now moved here from revenue.
statementNotes.pat@FY23: Profit +34% despite ₹1,105 cr of exceptional losses after tax.
statementNotes.sales@FY24: Revenue +16%: automotive +24% (SUVs), farm −2% (tractors −7% in a weak-monsoon year).
statementNotes.ebitda@FY24: EBITDA +24%: auto PBIT margin up from 4.8% to 8.4%.
statementNotes.otherIncome@FY24: Includes ₹2,456 cr of dividends and other income from group companies (moved from revenue); write-downs only ₹253 cr.
statementNotes.pat@FY24: Profit +62%: auto margins and a low-write-down year.
statementNotes.ebitda@FY25: EBITDA +32%: SUV mix and tractor margins near 18%.
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY25: Core margin 14.7%: SUV mix and farm PBIT margin 18.4%.
statementNotes.dep@FY25: D&A +21%: new models capitalised (Thar Roxx, XUV 3XO) and e-SUV manufacturing lines.
statementNotes.otherIncome@FY25: Group income ₹2,141 cr and treasury income, less ₹848 cr of write-downs of group companies (international farm units and others).
statementNotes.sales@FY26: Revenue +25%: GST 2.0 from 22-Sep-2025; UVs +20%, tractors +24%; e-SUVs for MEAL ₹12,413 cr.
statementNotes.materialPct@FY26: Material cost ratio up ~2 points: e-SUVs built for MEAL at full value (₹12,413 cr) carry almost no margin.
statementNotes.ebitda@FY26: EBITDA +23%: volumes; margin 14.4% (−30bp) on e-SUV mix.
statementNotes.otherIncome@FY26: Treasury ₹2,451 cr + group income ₹2,190 cr − write-downs ₹677 cr − exceptional ₹104 cr.
statementNotes.pat@FY26: Profit +32%: volumes plus higher treasury income.
statementNotes.capex@FY27E: Chakan capacity (68k to 82k units a month) and NU_IQ/INGLO tooling; Nagpur from FY28.
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY27E: Q1 12.2% after 400-500bp of commodity inflation; recovery in H2 assumed.
statementNotes.dep@FY17: D&A +43%: higher amortisation of capitalised product development.
statementNotes.dep@FY19: D&A +26% as the Marazzo, Alturas and XUV300 platforms were capitalised (launched FY19).
statementNotes.investments@FY17: Investments +32%: higher liquid investments and group investments.
statementNotes.payables@FY20: Payables −30%: production cut in the slowdown and March 2020 lockdown.
statementNotes.payables@FY21: Payables +57%: production recovered sharply in H2FY21.
statementNotes.payables@FY25: Payables +26% with revenue +18% and production at capacity.
statementNotes.payables@FY26: Payables +26%: suppliers fund working capital (₹29,500 cr vs inventory ₹10,306 cr).
statementNotes.cfo@FY18: Operating cash +77%: profit growth and payables.
statementNotes.cfo@FY21: Operating cash +161%: payables up ₹3,856 cr and lower inventory build in the COVID year.
statementNotes.cfo@FY26: Operating cash +37% (₹22,758 cr): profit +32% and payables +₹6,094 cr.
statementNotes.capex@FY23: Capex +30%: SUV capacity at Chakan and Nashik.
statementNotes.otherIncome@Q3FY24: Lower than Q2: group dividends ₹449 cr vs ₹1,367 cr (Tech Mahindra and M&M Finance pay in Q2).
statementNotes.opm@Q1FY25: Margin 15% (Q4FY24 12%): a seasonally strong tractor quarter.
statementNotes.sales@Q3FY25: Revenue +21%: festive season in October and SUV volumes.
statementNotes.ebitda@Q3FY25: EBITDA +40% YoY: volumes and SUV mix.
statementNotes.otherIncome@Q3FY25: Group dividends fall back to ₹426 cr after Q2.
statementNotes.ebitda@Q4FY25: EBITDA +51% YoY on a weak Q4FY24 base (margin 12%).
statementNotes.otherIncome@Q4FY25: Write-downs of group companies of ₹719 cr in the quarter.
statementNotes.pat@Q4FY25: Profit +22% YoY despite ₹719 cr of write-downs.
statementNotes.sales@Q1FY26: Revenue +26%: SUVs +22% (Q1FY26 a record share quarter), tractors +10%.
statementNotes.otherIncome@Q1FY26: Write-downs ₹148 cr; low group dividends (₹60 cr).
statementNotes.sales@Q2FY26: Revenue +21%: buyers delayed purchases in Aug-Sep 2025 ahead of the GST cut from 22-Sep-2025.
statementNotes.ebitda@Q2FY26: EBITDA +25% YoY; farm PBIT margin 24% (Navratri in September).
statementNotes.sales@Q4FY26: Revenue +26%: record UVs and tractors (Navratri in March).
statementNotes.pat@Q4FY26: Profit +53% YoY on a Q4FY25 base hit by ₹719 cr of write-downs.
statementNotes.opm@Q1FY27: Margin 12.2% (−210bp YoY): 400-500bp of commodity inflation in auto, 300bp+ in farm, ~85bp hedging loss.
